key_insight: The paper extends variance-reduced conditional gradient optimization to nonconvex composite problems when gradients are observed along a single Markov chain trajectory, using a clipped multilevel momentum Frank-Wolfe scheme with provable Markovian bias control.
engineering_relevance: This enables projection-free stochastic optimization for constrained ML and PDE-inspired models when data arrive sequentially and are correlated, which is closer to many real sampling and simulation pipelines than i.i.d. settings.
method: MC-ALFCG combines momentum conditional gradients with coupled capped multilevel Monte Carlo gradient estimates.
It uses consecutive samples from one Markov trajectory plus clipping to bound bias and stabilize adaptive updates.
The analysis reduces Markovian sampling to an independent-sampling recursion with mixing-time-dependent constants.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical sample-complexity guarantees and controlled numerical studies on dependence sensitivity, a nonconvex composite instance, and clipping behavior.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on a fixed ergodic transition kernel, mixing-time estimates, and clipping/coupling design choices, so performance may be sensitive to chain behavior and tuning in practice.
paper_title: Variance-Reduced Conditional Gradient Methods under Markovian Sampling for Nonconvex Composite Optimization
